newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Roman Catholic hierarchy and the gay community strongly object to the implementation of the national identification system (ALL PAPERS)
- About 50 persons were injured, some of them seriously, when more than 500 squatter residents in Binondo clashed with 200 demolition crewmen (TODAY)
- Congressmen complain about a report that policemen were monitoring 70 of them for possible contacts with fugitive congressman Romeo Jalosjos (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and President Fidel Ramos pledge to exert greater efforts to attain the full potential of their economic ties which have already increased by six-fold over the last few years (MANILA STANDARD)

- Socioeconomic planning secretary Cielito Habito says there is no need to alter the 1997 inflation targets of 6.0 to 6.5 percent this year despite the impending fuel price and wage increases (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The Central Bank plans to expand the current $25,000 over the counter dollar sales limit for banks to around $300,000 as part of its continuing liberalisation of the foreign exhcange market. (BUSINESS DAILY)

- The Board of Investments is planning to discontinue the granting of tax incentives to new and expanding industrial estates in Cavite and Laguna to encourage more industrial estates to be developed in other parts of the country. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
